Putin is allegedly worth $200 billion. His official salary is about $140,000 a year, and his declared property is one apartment and two old Soviet cars.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The $200B figure comes from investor-turned-Kremlin critic Bill Browder, who told the US Senate in 2017 Putin had amassed that much. Economist Anders Åslund puts it nearer $100-130B. A former Kremlin adviser estimated $70B back in 2012. No one has the paper trail.

2/ Gaddafi's $200B is mostly Libya's money, not his. When the UN froze Libyan assets in March 2011, it froze about $200B held by the Central Bank of Libya and the Libyan Investment Authority — sovereign wealth, not a personal account with his name on it.

3/ Mubarak estimates span an absurd range: US intelligence once put his real overseas cash at $1-5B, Egyptian media claimed up to $70B, and one widely mocked 2011 report claimed $700B including gold held at the US Federal Reserve. Courts never proved most of it.

4/ Saleh is the one figure here with real paperwork behind it. A 2015 UN Panel of Experts investigation put his fortune at $32-60B, built through decades of skimming Yemen's oil and gas contracts and customs revenue — a rare case where the number has a source.

5/ Every name on this map ruled a country too poor to explain fortunes this size. None of them ever had to. The gap between the number people repeat and the number anyone can actually prove is the real story here.
